title: Use two disjoint projections and a full homotopy to halve filling support
statement: For the admitted RX replacement, explicit p0,p1 have disjoint degree-one coordinates, wt(p0 e)+wt(p1 e)<=wt(e) on ALL vectors. With p_b F=I and I-F p_b=d h1+h2 d, one X-sector projection halves support while transposed repetition/homotopy pays the other sector. Alternating RX/RZ gives g_k(M)<=A(1+A)M+A²g_(k-1)(floor(M/2)), hence K M^p with p=ceil(log2(2A²)), K=max(seed bound,2A(1+A)); the full Pauli group uses2K M^p.

requires: The actual Balasubramanian-Davydova-Lin2605.10943v1 alternating family, fixed odd subdivision ell>=3, natural unique cancellation squares and specified planar seed
All-level size-two X/Z intersections, positive color incidences, connected check links and source degree bounds D7,E4
provides: Accepted depth-independent check-soundness and explicit filling algorithm at the actual recursive family
assumptions: Minimal GENERATOR COUNT for stabilizers is not syndrome expansion of arbitrary errors
Full all-vector homotopy is needed before transposing; a cocycle-only decoder would not suffice
Actual row/column cost orientation, natural squares and fixed ell are retained; small finite ranks do not establish the theorem
costs: Constants A,K,p depend on the fixed actual ell/degree bounds, not recursion depth; primary illustrative ell/packing constants enormous
Finite consumers ell3/5 do not acquire random spatial embedding or substitute for primary-qualified ell
Ordinary exact GF2 elimination already fills finite stabilizers in polynomial time; this is a uniform support/generator-count bridge, not a measured finite speedup
contract.units: Binary support weights and generator counts, exact F2 cochain maps, fixed subdivision constants and all recursion depths.
contract.obstruction: Finite elimination and passing matrix ranks do not by themselves give a support-count bound uniform in recursion depth.
